sections.h2: Which Rochester Hills offices handle the tax bill?
sections.html:
The city's Treasury Division mails the statements and receives payment, while the Assessing Department sets the values the bills are built on. In the March after the tax year, unpaid balances move to the Oakland County Treasurer in Pontiac. Rochester Hills sits in Oakland County, about 25 miles north of downtown Detroit, so most owners deal with a city office first and the county office only if a bill goes delinquent.

The Treasury page lists where the money goes. Local schools, Oakland Community College, the Oakland Schools intermediate district, the county, county parks, the Detroit Zoo, the Art Institute and Oakland Transit all take a share. The city's own portion pays for roads, fire, the library, the OPC Social and Activity Center and the Rochester Avon Recreation Authority. Police service is not a city department here, because the Oakland County Sheriff's Office patrols the city under contract.

  • Assessing Department, 1000 Rochester Hills Drive, Rochester Hills, MI 48309: 248-656-4605.
  • Treasury: 248-656-4675.
  • Oakland County Register of Deeds, for deed changes: 248-858-0581.
  • Oakland County Treasurer, for delinquent bills: 248-858-0611.

sections.h2: When are Rochester Hills property taxes due?
sections.html:
Two bills arrive each year, a summer bill and a winter bill, and each has a payment window that closes in mid-September or mid-February. The summer bill covers school and county taxes only, so the city's own levies fall on the winter bill.

Rochester Hills tax bill calendar, from the city Treasury property tax page
BillPayment windowIf paid late
SummerJuly 1 to September 14 (the 2026 deadline)1% interest on September 15, then 1% more each following month
WinterDecember 1 to mid-February (February 16 for the 2026 bill)3% penalty added after the deadline
Unpaid after bothDelinquent from March 2Payable to the Oakland County Treasurer with added penalties

The city does not honor postmarks. A check dropped in the mail on the due date counts as late, so use the black drop box at City Hall, pay online or walk it in. Online payment by e-check carries no fee, and cards carry a 2.75% processing fee and never less than $1.50. First State Bank also takes cash or check, but you must hand over the whole tax bill. Enrollment in recurring automatic payment, which draws on a bank account, costs nothing.

sections.h2: How can an owner lower or delay the tax bill?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills offers a summer tax deferment for owners with limited income. The city form tied to a 2025 deadline set the household income ceiling at $40,000 and listed these groups:

  • Owners aged 62 or older, including an unremarried surviving spouse.
  • Paraplegic or quadriplegic owners.
  • Eligible service members, veterans and widows.
  • Blind owners.
  • Totally and permanently disabled owners.

Applicants file the city form together with a copy of their Michigan Homestead Property Tax Credit claim. The filing date moves each year, so ask Treasury for the current form and deadline. Disabled veterans can also ask about the exemption in MCL 211.7b, which the city links from both its tax and deferment pages.

For the amount of the bill itself, the lever is the assessment. The Assessing Department mails notices in February, and a homeowner who finds the value too steep books an appointment before the Board of Review in March. Under state law the board convenes in the second week of March, and the board must send each protester a written decision, with Michigan Tax Tribunal appeal details, ahead of the first Monday of June (MCL 211.30).

sections.h2: What happens to the taxable value when a Rochester Hills house sells?
sections.html:
The buyer's taxable value resets to the state equalized value the year after the sale. Until then, taxable value climbs each year by no more than the smaller of 5% or inflation, and it can never exceed the state equalized value (MCL 211.27a). A seller who has lived in the house for many years may have a much lower bill than the buyer will, and the difference is worth knowing before a listing goes up.

The city's assessing FAQ gives owners a rough way to forecast a bill: take half of the estimated property value and multiply by the current millage rate. For an addition, it suggests treating half the project cost as added taxable value. Its example is a $30,000 project, which adds $15,000 of taxable value before the millage is applied.

After closing, the buyer should receive a Property Transfer Affidavit and a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit from the closing agent. Both go to the Assessors Office at City Hall, staffed on weekdays from morning to late afternoon. State law gives the buyer 45 days from the transfer to report it to the assessor.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the city itself?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills became a city in 1984, when Avon Township voters approved a charter and chose the name over the alternative, Avon Hills. Its 32.9 square miles are almost entirely land, bounded by Troy to the south, Auburn Hills to the west, Shelby Township in Macomb County to the east and Oakland Township to the north. The 2020 census counted 76,300 residents and 31,208 housing units, of which 4.8% stood vacant.

Rochester Community Schools covers the larger share of the city and operates Rochester Adams, Rochester and Stoney Creek high schools. Avondale School District covers some of the rest, and the district printed on the bill sets the school millage. Oakland University and Rochester Christian University also have programs in the city.

A seller behind on taxes has a practical path. Ask Treasury for the exact balance and the penalty clock, get a payoff statement from the title agent, and have the unpaid amount paid off through the closing statement. If the bill has already gone to Oakland County, call the county treasurer at 248-858-0611, since the city bill carries a notice pointing owners to county hardship help.

sections.h2: What does the county take over after March 1?
sections.html:
Any balance still open on March 2 belongs to Oakland County, not the city, and the city's pay options no longer apply. Tax bills carry a notice if prior year taxes were returned delinquent, pointing the owner to the county treasurer's hardship line. Interest and penalties keep growing, so anyone selling a parcel with delinquent tax should clear it before listing or build the payoff into the closing statement.

For a deed with warranty covenants, state law has the register of deeds ask for a county treasurer certificate that no tax liens exist and that taxes for the five preceding years are paid (MCL 211.135). A quitclaim deed with no warranty is excepted from that rule. Either way, a clean tax history keeps a sale moving.

faqs.q: Which number reaches the Rochester Hills assessor?
faqs.a: Dial 248-656-4605 for the Assessing Department. It handles values, name and address changes, and the Principal Residence Exemption. The office is at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive, inside City Hall.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if I miss the Rochester Hills summer deadline?
faqs.a: Interest of 1% attaches the day after the deadline and a further 1% attaches each month after that. The city also adds a 3% penalty after the mid-February winter deadline. Postmarks are not honored.

faqs.q: Does a sale change the next tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. A transfer of ownership resets the taxable value to the state equalized value for the year after the sale. A buyer who inherits a long-held house can see a noticeably higher bill than the seller paid.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Rochester Hills tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes, online, by phone or at the Treasurer's office, with a 2.75% processing fee and a $1.50 minimum. E-check online is free. Checks go in the drop box at City Hall or by mail.

faqs.q: Where do delinquent Rochester Hills taxes go?
faqs.a: They go to the Oakland County Treasurer, 1200 N. Telegraph, Pontiac, MI 48341, from March 2. The county treasurer's number printed on the bill is 248-858-0611.
